nl.statement: Two-population full-data potential-outcome world at index n: P_n^F is a probability Measure on the explicit coordinate space FullData := Bool x X x Bool x Bool x R x R carrying (S, X, D(0), D(1), Y(0), Y(1)); the assignment potential outcome is the derived map Y^Z(z) = Y(D(z)); the forced parameter space is Theta = Set.Icc (-1 : R) 1 and the causal target theta_T is the complier-conditional contrast under S = 0. — Bypass-justified (see decisions.full_data_coordinate_space): Causalean.PO's POSystem/POIVSystem is a regime- and variable-indexed skeleton with no population indicator and no transport layer, and the least-favourable witness must be built explicitly and checked against every causal assumption, which is only tractable on an explicit coordinate law. Causalean.PO.ID.Exact.LATE.POIVSystem (late_wald and its four-step chain) is the ANALOGOUS module F3 should adapt for prop:compact-causal-range; gap to bridge = two populations + the transport change of measure. PO/ID/Exact/LATE.lean'; grepped ../Causalean for 'transport', 'population indicator', 'S = 0', 'POIVSystem'; scanned ../Causalean/PO/{Core,Assumptions,ID/Exact} -- no two-population transported potential-outcome world: not found.

Observed two-sample triangular-array sampling world: n i.i.d. source observations O_i^S = (X_i, Z_i, D_i, Y_i) ~ P_S on X x Bool x Bool x R, independently N_n i.i.d. target covariate draws X_j^T ~ P_T on X, with N_n / n -> c; the joint sample law at index n is Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin n => P_S) .prod (Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin N_n => P_T)). P_S is the observed-data law induced by P_n^F given S = 1 with source assignment propensity e, P_S^X its X-marginal, P_T the S = 0 X-marginal, and e : X -> R the source propensity taking values in [eps, 1 - eps]. — The i.i.d. primitives are reused (Causalean.Stat.IIDSample, Causalean.Stat.iidSample_infinitePi, Causalean.Stat.iidSample_finN_pushforward give the coordinate-projection sample and its Measure.pi pushforward), but the world itself is a PRODUCT of two independent samples with DIFFERENT laws (source observations vs covariate-only target draws) and an index-linked size N_n, which IIDSample does not package -- so the two-sample world is define-local over Mathlib Measure.pi/Measure.prod on top of the reused primitives. Transport / overlap geometry world: the deterministic array g = (P_S^X, w, e)_{n>=1} with w : X -> R the density ratio dP_T/dP_S^X normalized by E_S[w(X)] = 1 and capped by 0 <= w <= 2 k_n, the Kish dispersion kappa_n = E_S[w(X)^2] <= k_n, the known envelope sequence k_n, and (in the cell submodels) the known source-cell probability array q_{x,n} = P_S^X{x} with c_- / k_n <= q_{x,n} <= c_+ / k_n. — Plain measurable-function / real-scalar geometry layer over Mathlib (Measure.rnDeriv for w = dP_T/dP_S^X plus the P_T(A) = E_S[w 1_A] change-of-measure identity). Search trace: grepped ../Causalean for 'densityRatio', 'density ratio', 'covariate shift', 'Kish', 'importance weight', 'rnDeriv' in Stat/ and Estimation/; scanned ../doc/API.md sections 12/13sa/13eff -- Causalean carries Measure.rnDeriv plumbing (Stat/Minimax/ChiSquared.rnDeriv_prod_eq, Mathlib/CondDistrib) but no transport-weight / Kish-dispersion geometry object: not found.

Identification and effective-strength scalar world: the two identified source conditional contrasts Delta_Y, Delta_D : X -> R, their transported means mu_{Y,n} = E_S[w Delta_Y] and mu_n = E_S[w Delta_D] > 0, the effective identification strength t_n = n mu_n^2 / kappa_n, the frontier argument t_0 > 0, the noncoverage level alpha in (0,1), the Le Cam calibration rho = (1 - alpha) / 8, and the frontier constants c_0, C_0, t_c. — Real-valued functionals of (P_S, w) plus plain real scalars; realized as named defs over Mathlib integrals. Procedure and minimax-risk world: a confidence-set sequence is a bundled random subset C_n of Theta -- a map from the index-n sample (plus the declared oracle/known inputs) to Set R with a jointly measurable graph and C_n subset Theta -- with lambda = MeasureTheory.volume restricted to Theta as the length; on top of it the four honest procedure classes (oracle, fixed-geometry oracle, finite-cell feasible, regular-cell feasible), the four model classes / slices (P_n, N_n, N_n^reg, P_n(g)), the worst-case limiting risk R, and the three value functions V*, V*_N, V*_g. — Analogous modules, not exact fits. Causalean.Estimation.MinimaxATE.Model gives the inf-sup packaging shape (minimaxMiss = iSup over a subtype of in-class DGPs, bddAbove_nMiss_range, nMiss_le_minimaxMiss) which is copied verbatim in shape, but its risk is a finite-PMF quantile MISS probability, not honest expected SET LENGTH, and its class is a finite-X ATE nuisance ball. Causalean.PO.ID.Partial.Inference.Basic gives coverage vocabulary (RandomCoversPoint, honest_ci_set_cover) for a fixed interval-identified parameter with plug-in half-widths, not an inf over honest procedure SEQUENCES with a limsup-of-sup risk. Unfolding kishDispersion yields ∫w(x)^2 dP_S^X, exactly κ_n, so the Lean inequality is precisely κ_n ≤ k_n.
The three conjuncts respectively encode k_n→+∞, k_n/√n→0, and μ_n=∫w(x)Δ_D(x)dP_S^X→0, exactly the stated degrading-array conditions.

nl.statement: \(\mathcal P_n=\{P=(P_n^F,e):P\text{ satisfies ass:full-data-support, ass:population-presence, ass:two-sample-array, ass:instrument-overlap, ass:source-observation, ass:iv-randomization, ass:iv-exclusion, ass:iv-monotonicity, ass:outcome-transport, ass:receipt-transport, ass:target-complier-positivity, ass:transport-domination, ass:weight-envelope, ass:weight-second-moment, and ass:degrading-array at index }n\}\).

review.note: FiniteCellClass is the flattened conjunction defining TransportedIVClass together with FiniteCellSource, so it is equivalent in both directions to P ∈ 𝒫_n plus the finite-cell assumption.

nl.frozen_body:
The oracle honest class is the class of oracle procedures \((C_n)_{n\ge1}\) satisfying \(0<\alpha<1\) and the following conditions.  For every \(n\), \(C_n\) maps each input
\[
\left((O_i^S)_{i=1}^n,(X_j^T)_{j=1}^{N_n},w,e\right),
\qquad
w:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R,\quad w(x)\ge0,\quad e:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R,
\]
to a subset of \(\Theta=[-1,1]\).  For every \(n\) and every measurable such pair \((w,e)\), the sample-by-parameter graph
\[
\left\{
\left(((O_i^S)_{i=1}^n,(X_j^T)_{j=1}^{N_n}),\vartheta\right):
\vartheta\in
C_n\!\left((O_i^S)_{i=1}^n,(X_j^T)_{j=1}^{N_n},w,e\right)
\right\}
\]
is measurable.  For every \(n\), every \(P\in\mathcal P_n\), and every pair \(w,w'\) of measurable nonnegative versions of \(dP_T/dP_S^X\), the evaluations using the row-\(n\) propensity score agree for the two-sample law almost surely:
\[
C_n\!\left((O_i^S)_{i=1}^n,(X_j^T)_{j=1}^{N_n},w,e\right)
=
C_n\!\left((O_i^S)_{i=1}^n,(X_j^T)_{j=1}^{N_n},w',e\right).
\]
Finally,
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle \inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n}
P\!\left(\theta_T\in C_n\right), & \mathcal P_n\neq\varnothing,\\[0.8em]
1, & \mathcal P_n=\varnothing
\end{cases}
\ge 1-\alpha,
\]
where in the probability term \(C_n\) is evaluated at the canonical row-\(n\) density ratio \(dP_T/dP_S^X\) and the row-\(n\) propensity score.

review.note: Unfolding OracleProcedure, oracleCoverageClassInf, and oracleCoverage yields exactly sample-and-(w,e)-indexed measurable subsets of Θ with the stated liminf uniform-coverage condition; alpha's range is the declared global domain, and a.e.-weight invariance conservatively enforces the intrinsic Radon–Nikodym quotient.

Unfolding frontierRiskTotal and frontierRiskRow gives limsup_n of the supremum over precisely P ∈ 𝒫_n satisfying effectiveStrength P n ≥ t₀ of the expected Lebesgue length, on the paper's declared domain t₀ > 0.

nl.frozen_body:
For any fixed effective-strength threshold \(t_0\) with \(0<t_0\), the oracle minimax expected-length value is
\[
V^\star(t_0)
=
\inf_{(C_n)\in\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{or}}}
R((C_n),t_0).
\]

review.note: Unfolding oracleValueTotal and frontierRiskTotal gives exactly the infimum over globally oracle-honest procedures of the paper's limsup worst-case expected-length risk on t0 > 0.

Unfolding finiteCellOracleValueTotal and finiteCellOracleRisk gives exactly the infimum over the global oracle-honest class of the limsup supremum restricted to P in the finite-cell class with effectiveStrength >= t0.

FiniteCellProcedure supplies precisely sample-only sets contained in Theta, while FiniteCellHonest is the stated liminf rowwise-infimum coverage condition; the alpha bounds are the paper's declared domain, and coverageInfOrOne preserves the honesty inequality on empty rows.

nl.statement: For every \(\vartheta\in\Theta\), form the source inverse-propensity score \(w(X)\{Z/e(X)-(1-Z)/(1-e(X))\}(Y-\vartheta D)\), compare its empirical mean with \(L_\alpha\{n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nw(X_i)^2/n\}^{1/2}\), and invert the resulting acceptance inequality over \(\Theta\).  Once \(w\) and \(e\) are oracle-known, the target sample does not enter this score.

review.note: Unfolding the score means, instrument score, empiricalKish, and parameterSpace yields the inverse-propensity empirical score for Y-theta*D, threshold L*sqrt((n^-1 sum w_i^2)/n), inversion over [-1,1], and no target-sample input.

nl.statement:
Hold an arbitrary admissible deterministic array \((P_S^X,w,e)\) fixed, set \(\mu_n=(t_0\kappa_n/n)^{1/2}\) and the conditional complier probability \(p_n(x)=\mu_nw(x)/\kappa_n\).  For \(0<\alpha<1\), set \(\rho=(1-\alpha)/8\), vary only the complier outcome mean over the continuum \(h\in\mathbb R\) satisfying \(|h|\le\min\{1/4,\rho t_0^{-1/2}\}\), and compare every member with its center according to
\[
 1+\chi^2(Q_{n,h}^{\mathfrak g}\Vert Q_{n,0}^{\mathfrak g})\le\exp(8t_0h^2),
 \qquad
 \|Q_{n,h}^{\mathfrak g}-Q_{n,0}^{\mathfrak g}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le2\rho.
\]

review.note: Unfolding geometryMu, geometryKish, geometryCompliance, and leastFavorableWitness gives the paper's admissible fixed geometry, mu_n and p_n formulas, rho and h domain, continuum varying the complier outcome mean, and the stated chi-square and total-variation comparisons; the probability-validity and exact moment/strength conjuncts express consequences and well-definedness of that same construction.

nl.statement: Fix \(\mathfrak g=(P_S^X,w,e)_{n\ge1}\in\mathcal G\) and \(t_0>0\).  Set \(\mu_n=(t_0\kappa_n/n)^{1/2}\), \(p_n(x)=\mu_nw(x)/\kappa_n\), \(\rho=(1-\alpha)/8\), and \(H(t_0)=\min\{1/4,\rho t_0^{-1/2}\}\).  Conditional on \(X=x\), assign compliance types \((D(0),D(1))=(0,1),(1,1),(0,0)\) probabilities \(p_n(x),(1-p_n(x))/2,(1-p_n(x))/2\).  Set \(Y(0)=0\); for compliers let \(Y(1)\) be Bernoulli \((1/2+h)\), and for both always-takers and never-takers let \(Y(1)\) be Bernoulli \((1/2)\), for \(|h|\le H(t_0)\).  Use this same conditional full-data law in both populations, draw source encouragement with propensity \(e(X)\), and denote the resulting joint observed-data law and fixed oracle inputs by \(Q_{n,h}^{\mathfrak g}\).

review.note: After unfolding the geometry formulas and fixedGeometrySlice, binary Y1 support plus the type-probability and type-specific first-moment identities determine exactly the stated conditional Bernoulli laws a.e.; the shared kernel, source assignment, first stage, strength, and CACE clauses encode equivalent consequences of that construction.

nl.statement: \(\mathcal G\) is the class of deterministic arrays \(\mathfrak g=(P_S^X,w,e)_{n\ge1}\) such that \(P_S^X\) is a probability law on \(\mathcal X\), \(e:\mathcal X\to[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\), \(w:\mathcal X\to[0,2k_n]\), \(\mathbb E_S[w(X)]=1\), \(\kappa_n=\mathbb E_S[w(X)^2]\le k_n\), and \(P_T(A)=\mathbb E_S[w(X)\mathbf 1\{X\in A\}]\) for every measurable \(A\subseteq\mathcal X\).

review.note: The clauses reproduce the source-law, propensity, weight, normalization, second-moment, and weighted target-law conditions; target probability follows from normalization, while measurability and 0<epsilon<1/2 are part of the declared global domains.

nl.statement: For \(\mathfrak g\in\mathcal G\), \(\mathcal P_n(\mathfrak g)=\{P\in\mathcal P_n:(P_S^X,w,e)\text{ equals the index-}n\text{ component of }\mathfrak g\}\).

review.note: Unfolding fixedGeometrySlice gives membership in the main class and equality of the source law, propensity, and density-ratio representative at row n; target-law equality is redundant because the admissible geometry and Radon–Nikodym weight uniquely induce it, and weight equality is correctly a.e.

The subtype ranges over exactly the fixed-geometry slice, fixedGeometryOracleCoverage is the stated coverage probability, and the liminf rowwise coverage infimum is equivalent to the paper condition; coverageInfOrOne preserves the empty-row truth value under 0<alpha<1.

nl.statement: \(V_{\mathfrak g}^\star(t_0)=\inf_{(C_n)\in\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{or}}(\mathfrak g)}\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n(\mathfrak g):\,t_n\ge t_0}\mathbb E_P[\lambda(C_n)]\).

review.note: Unfolding fixedGeometryValueTotal, fixedGeometryRisk, and fixedGeometryOracleExpectedLength yields exactly the infimum over fixed-geometry honest oracle procedures of the limsup rowwise supremum over slice laws with effectiveStrength at least t0, with t0 restricted to the paper's positive domain.

nl.statement: \(\mathcal N_n^{\mathrm{reg}}=\{P\in\mathcal P_n:P_S^X\text{ is supported on exactly }k_n\text{ measurable cells},\;q_{x,n}=P_S^X(X\text{ lies in cell }x),\;c_-/k_n\le q_{x,n}\le c_+/k_n\text{ for every }x\}\), where \(0<c_-\le1\le c_+<\infty\) are fixed.

review.note: After unfolding TransportedIVClass and sourceXLaw, the injected measurable singleton support has full source mass and exactly k n positive-mass cells, while the toReal bounds are precisely cminus/k n ≤ q_{x,n} ≤ cplus/k n; the explicit positivity and ordering clauses state the paper's fixed-constant domain.

nl.frozen_body:
For a noncoverage level \(0<\alpha<1\), define \(\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{reg}}\) as the class of regular-cell procedures \((C_n)_{n\ge 1}\) with the following properties. For each \(n\), \(C_n\) is a \(\Theta\)-valued random set whose inputs are \((O_i^S)_{i=1}^n\), \((X_j^T)_{j=1}^{N_n}\), the realized regular-cell support, and the known cell-indexed vectors \((q_{x,n})_{x=1}^{k_n}\) and \((e_{x,n})_{x=1}^{k_n}\). For every realized regular-cell support and every pair of real \(k_n\)-vectors \((q_{x,n})_{x=1}^{k_n}\) and \((e_{x,n})_{x=1}^{k_n}\), the sample-by-\(\theta\) graph of \(C_n\), restricted to source and target samples on that support, is measurable. These procedures satisfy
\[
1-\alpha\le
\liminf_{n\to\infty}
\inf_{P\in\mathcal N_n^{\mathrm{reg}}}
P(\theta_T\in C_n),
\]
with the rowwise infimum evaluated as \(1\) when \(\mathcal N_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\) is empty.

review.note: RegularCellProcedure exposes exactly the two samples, labeled finite support with its known q and e vectors, and sets contained in Θ but no w; regularCellCoverage is the stated coverage probability, and coverageInfOrOne preserves the honesty inequality on empty rows while the liminf and rowwise infimum match the paper.

nl.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal P_n\), source randomization identifies \(\Delta_Y(x)=\mathbb E_{P_n^F}[Y^Z(1)-Y^Z(0)\mid X=x,S=1]\) and \(\Delta_D(x)=\mathbb E_{P_n^F}[D(1)-D(0)\mid X=x,S=1]\). Outcome-contrast transport and integrated first-stage transport imply \(\mu_{Y,n}=\mathbb E_{P_n^F}[(Y(1)-Y(0))\mathbf 1\{D(1)>D(0)\}\mid S=0]\) and \(\mu_n=P_n^F(D(1)>D(0)\mid S=0)\). Hence \(\mu_{Y,n}/\mu_n=\theta_T=\mathbb E_{P_n^F}[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid D(1)>D(0),S=0]\in\Theta=[-1,1]\).

review.note: After unfolding the representation and causal-functional definitions, the two measurable-set integral characterizations encode the source conditional contrasts a.e.; the transported moments equal the target complier numerator and share, targetCACE is their positive-denominator conditional-effect ratio, and parameterSpace is exactly [-1,1]. The two explicit source-integrability premises are consequences of TransportedIVClass and therefore do not restrict the paper domain.

nl.statement: There exist constants \(c_0>0\) and \(t_c>0\), depending only on \(\alpha\), \(\varepsilon\), and the fixed class constants, such that for every \(t_0>0\), \(V^\star(t_0)\ge c_0\min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\}\) and \(V_{\mathcal N}^\star(t_0)\ge c_0\min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\}\). In particular, \(V^\star(t_0)\ge c_0\) whenever \(0<t_0\le t_c\). The constants do not depend on the decomposition of \(t_0\) into \(\mu_n\) and \(\kappa_n\).

review.note: After unfolding both oracle value definitions, Lean gives exactly both lower frontiers and the small-threshold global bound on t₀>0; the PositiveThreshold subtype is equivalent to the paper domain, and binding c₀,t_c before 𝒳,N,k,t₀ encodes the claimed decomposition-independent uniform constants.

nl.statement: If \(w(X)=1\) \(P_S\)-almost surely, then \(\kappa_n=1\) and \(t_n=n\mu_n^2\); hence the frontier specializes to compact single-population weak-ratio inference.

review.note: Unfolding the definitions, w=1 source-a.e. gives geometryKish=1 and targetX=sourceX; fixedGeometrySlice transfers this to κ_n=1 and effectiveStrength=nμ_n², while fixedGeometryValue is the compact Θ=[-1,1] slice frontier and its displayed bounds exactly instantiate the paper’s fixed-geometry and score-inversion constants.

nl.statement:
Let
\[
 H_i=\frac{Z_i}{e(X_i)}-\frac{1-Z_i}{1-e(X_i)},\quad
 \widehat A_n=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^nw(X_i)H_iY_i,\quad
 \widehat B_n=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^nw(X_i)H_iD_i,
\]
and \(\widehat\kappa_n=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nw(X_i)^2\).  With \(L_\alpha=\{8/(\alpha\varepsilon^2)\}^{1/2}\), define the single score-inversion sequence
\[
 C_n=\left\{\vartheta\in\Theta:
 |\widehat A_n-\vartheta\widehat B_n|
 \le L_\alpha\sqrt{\widehat\kappa_n/n}\right\}.
\]
Then \((C_n)\in\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{or}}\), and, simultaneously for every \(t_0>0\),
\[
 R((C_n),t_0)\le C_0\min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\},
 \qquad
 C_0=\max\left\{2,4L_\alpha+\frac8{\varepsilon^2}\right\}.
\]
Consequently \(V^\star(t_0)\) has order \(\min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\}\).  The displayed upper bound holds for every admissible weight geometry and depends on a member law through \(t_n=n\mu_n^2/\kappa_n\) only, apart from the fixed constants.  Combined with the fixed-geometry frontier theorem, the achievability bound and the conditional converse match in order uniformly over admissible geometries, so any two admissible geometries with the same effective strength are equally difficult up to universal constants.

On \(\mathcal N_n\), write
\[
 H_i=2(2Z_i-1),\qquad
 \widehat p_{x,n}=\frac1{N_n}\sum_{j=1}^{N_n}\mathbf 1\{X_j^T=x\},
\]
and, for \(G\in\{Y,D\}\), define
\[
 \widehat m_{G,n}(x)=\frac{k_n}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n
 \mathbf 1\{X_i=x\}H_iG_i,\qquad
 \widehat M_{G,n}=\sum_{x=1}^{k_n}\widehat p_{x,n}\widehat m_{G,n}(x).
\]
For \(N_n\ge2\), let
\[
 \widehat\kappa_{U,n}=
 \frac{k_n}{N_n(N_n-1)}
 \sum_{j\ne\ell}\mathbf 1\{X_j^T=X_\ell^T\},\qquad
 \widehat K_n=1+\widehat\kappa_{U,n}.
\]
Put \(B_c=32(1+c^{-1})\), \(L_{\alpha,c}=\{2B_c/\alpha\}^{1/2}\), and
\[
 C_n=\left\{\vartheta\in\Theta:
 |\widehat M_{Y,n}-\vartheta\widehat M_{D,n}|
 \le L_{\alpha,c}\sqrt{\widehat K_n/n}\right\},
\]
with \(C_n=\Theta\) at the finitely many indices for which \(N_n<2\).  This sequence belongs to \(\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{cell}}\), does not use \(w\), and satisfies, simultaneously for all \(t_0>0\),
\[
 \limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{P\in\mathcal N_n:\,t_n\ge t_0}
 \mathbb E_P[\lambda(C_n)]
 \le C_0\min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\},
\]
where
\[
 C_0=\max\{2,4\sqrt2L_{\alpha,c}+8B_c\}.
\]
Moreover, the finite-cell change-of-measure family used for the oracle converse applies to every sequence in \(\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{cell}}\); hence the corresponding infimum of the displayed worst-case risk is at least \(c_0\min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\}\).  Thus estimating the target cell probabilities creates no additional minimax-order loss on \(\mathcal N_n\).

Let \(\mathfrak g\in\mathcal G\) be any admissible deterministic geometry array.  Put \(L_\alpha=\{8/(\alpha\varepsilon^2)\}^{1/2}\), \(c_\alpha=3(1-\alpha)^2/16\), and \(C_\alpha=\max\{2,4L_\alpha+8\varepsilon^{-2}\}\).  Then, for every fixed \(t_0>0\),
\[
 c_\alpha\min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\}
 \le V_{\mathfrak g}^\star(t_0)
 \le C_\alpha\min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\}.
\]
Both constants are uniform in \(\mathfrak g\).  In particular, after conditioning on any admissible source-covariate law, transport-weight array, and propensity array, geometries having the same effective strength are equally difficult up to the displayed universal constants.

On \(\mathcal N_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\), let \(q_{x,n}=P_S^X(X=x)\), let
\[
 H_i=\frac{Z_i}{e(X_i)}-\frac{1-Z_i}{1-e(X_i)},
 \qquad \widehat p_{x,n}=\frac1{N_n}\sum_{j=1}^{N_n}\mathbf 1\{X_j^T=x\},
\]
and, for \(G\in\{Y,D\}\), define
\[
 \widehat m_{G,n}(x)=\frac1{nq_{x,n}}\sum_{i=1}^n
 \mathbf 1\{X_i=x\}H_iG_i,
 \qquad
 \widehat M_{G,n}=\sum_{x=1}^{k_n}\widehat p_{x,n}\widehat m_{G,n}(x).
\]
For \(N_n\ge2\), set
\[
 \widehat\kappa_{U,n}=
 \frac1{N_n(N_n-1)}\sum_{j\ne\ell}
 \frac{\mathbf 1\{X_j^T=X_\ell^T\}}{q_{X_j^T,n}},
 \qquad \widehat K_n=1+\widehat\kappa_{U,n}.
\]
Put \(B_{\varepsilon,c}=8(\varepsilon^{-2}+c^{-1})\).  For every fixed \(L\ge\{2B_{\varepsilon,c}/\alpha\}^{1/2}\), the sequence
\[
 C_n^{\mathrm{reg}}=\left\{\vartheta\in\Theta:
 |\widehat M_{Y,n}-\vartheta\widehat M_{D,n}|
 \le L\sqrt{\widehat K_n/n}\right\},
\]
with \(C_n^{\mathrm{reg}}=\Theta\) when \(N_n<2\), belongs to \(\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{reg}}\), does not use \(w\), and satisfies, for every fixed \(t_0>0\),
\[
 \limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{P\in\mathcal N_n^{\mathrm{reg}}:\,t_n\ge t_0}
 \mathbb E_P[\lambda(C_n^{\mathrm{reg}})]
 \le \max\{2,4\sqrt2L+8B_{\varepsilon,c}\}
 \min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\}.
\]
The infimum of this risk over \(\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{reg}}\) is at least \(3(1-\alpha)^2\min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\}/16\).  Thus unknown target cell probabilities cause no minimax-order loss for known regular source-cell probabilities and a known cell-varying propensity bounded by \(\varepsilon\).
